in_hebrew.name: שולמיאל
in_hebrew.meaning: שולמיאל - השלום שלי, אלוהים הוא שלום
in_hebrew.long_meaning: שולמיאל הוא שם עברי שפירושו 'השלום שלי' או 'אלוהים הוא שלום'. השם מורכב משתי מילים: 'שלום' שפירושו שלום, ושם האל 'אל' או 'אלוהים'. השם שולמיאל מופיע בתנ"ך, בספר במדבר, פרק כ"ד, פסוק י"ד, כשם של אחד מנשיאי שבט אסר.

in_greek.name: Σουλαμιήλ
in_greek.meaning: Σουλαμιήλ - ειρήνη μου, ο Θεός είναι ειρήνη
in_greek.long_meaning: Σουλαμιήλ είναι ένα ελληνικό όνομα που σημαίνει 'η ειρήνη μου' ή 'ο Θεός είναι ειρήνη'. Το όνομα προέρχεται από τις εβραϊκές λέξεις 'שלום' (shalom) που σημαίνει ειρήνη και 'אל' (El) που σημαίνει Θεός. Το όνομα Σουλαμιήλ αναφέρεται στην Αγία Γραφή, στο βιβλίο των Αριθμών, κεφάλαιο 24, εδάφιο 14, ως το όνομα ενός από τους αρχηγούς της φυλής Ασήρ.

in_latin.name: Sulamiel
in_latin.meaning: Sulamiel - pax mea, Deus est pax
in_latin.long_meaning: Sulamiel est nomen hebraicum quod significat 'pax mea' vel 'Deus est pax'. Nomen componitur ex duabus vocibus: 'shalom' quod significat pacem, et 'El' seu 'Deus'. Nomen Sulamiel in Scriptura Sacra, in libro Numerorum, capitulo 24, versiculo 14, occurrit ut nomen unius ex principibus tribus Asher.

in_english.name: Sulamiel
in_english.meaning: Sulamiel means 'my peace' or 'God is peace'
in_english.long_meaning: Sulamiel is a Christian name derived from Hebrew roots, meaning 'my peace' or 'God is peace'. It is composed of two words: 'shalom' (peace) and 'El' (God). The name Sulamiel appears in the Bible, in the book of Numbers, chapter 24, verse 14, as the name of one of the princes of the tribe of Asher. The name carries a deep spiritual significance, symbolizing the peace and tranquility that comes from a relationship with God. In Christian tradition, Sulamiel is often associated with qualities such as calmness, serenity, and inner peace.

historical_references.reference: In Jewish folklore, Sulamiel is a beautiful angel who watches over infants and children. She is often depicted as a lovely young woman with a halo and wings, holding a lily or a rose.

In Christian tradition, Sulamiel is identified as the Virgin Mary under the title 'Our Lady of the Seven Sorrows'. This title refers to the seven swords of sorrow that pierced Mary's heart during Jesus' Passion and death. The devotion to Our Lady of the Seven Sorrows became popular during the late medieval period, around the 15th and 16th centuries.
